description:
## Problem
On 2026-11-22 in a fresh worktree of benchbox-site `next` (7e90968), `npm run docs:check` reported 11 blocking docs-contract violations, for example "option --timeout is not an option of benchbox run", "run_benchmark.timeout_seconds is documented but not a parameter" and "Current result schema version: `2.4`". CI on the same commit reported a different set of 3 (TPC-DI support status and query count). Locally, `docs:check` reads `DOCS_INPUTS` or, if unset, the committed `release-pin/` (`docsInputsRoot`, `website/src/lib/site-inputs.ts`), which is the `main` contract and predates the run-time-limit release; CI on `next` sets `DOCS_INPUTS=.site-inputs` after `npm run bundle:fetch` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). On a `next` branch, a contributor running the obvious command checks against the wrong contract, chases violations that are not real, and misses the real ones.

## Change
Make `docs:check` print which inputs it used (release pin or fetched bundle, with version or core commit). On a branch based on `next` with `DOCS_INPUTS` unset, also say that CI uses the fetched bundle and give the exact commands (`npm run bundle:fetch && DOCS_INPUTS=.site-inputs npm run docs:check`). Keep CI unchanged.

## Decision gates
- Placement: benchbox-site's AGENTS.md puts site-only work in benchbox-site's own tracker. Ask the owner whether to move this item there (then drop this copy with that reason) before implementing.
- Do not make the check pass by skipping contracts; fetching the bundle needs network access and a GitHub token, so never make the plain command fail offline.

## Verification rubric
Pass: on a `next` worktree with `DOCS_INPUTS` unset, `npm run docs:check` names the release-pin inputs and prints the CI-equivalent command; following it reproduces CI's result for the same commit; a test covers the message for both input sources.
Fail: the inputs used are still not shown.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree of BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site (`git -C /Users/joe/Developer/benchbox-site worktree add ../benchbox-site.wt-<slug> <branch>`); never edit `/Users/joe/Developer/benchbox-site` itself. benchbox-site has no Makefile; its checks are `npm run` scripts. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
